subject: ela
intro: Authors of informational texts make points, or claims, about a topic. They then give reasons to support those points. A reason explains why a point is true or why readers should believe it. Good readers can identify the author's main point and explain which reasons connect to it and why those reasons make the point stronger.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'You should drink water every day. Water helps your body stay cool when you are hot. It carries important nutrients through your blood. Without water, your body cannot work properly.'

What is the author's main point? Which reason best supports that point?

steps: I look for the main point. The first sentence says 'you should drink water every day.' That is the author's main point.
The other sentences give reasons. They say water cools your body, carries nutrients, and that you need water to work properly.
All three reasons support the main point, but the strongest is that without water your body cannot work properly.
That reason supports the point most directly because it shows that drinking water is not just helpful but necessary.
solution.answer: The author's main point is that you should drink water every day. The strongest supporting reason is that without water, your body cannot work properly. This shows that water is essential, not just helpful, which makes the point very convincing.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Dogs make wonderful family pets. They are loyal and love spending time with their owners. Dogs can also be trained to follow commands, which makes them safe around children. Studies show that people with dogs feel less lonely.'

What is the author's main point? Name two reasons the author gives to support it.

steps: The main point is in the first sentence: 'Dogs make wonderful family pets.'
The author gives three reasons. First, dogs are loyal. Second, dogs can be trained. Third, people with dogs feel less lonely.
Two reasons that support the main point are: dogs can be trained to follow commands (making them safe) and people with dogs feel less lonely.
Both reasons show why dogs are good for families.
solution.answer: The author's main point is that dogs make wonderful family pets. Two supporting reasons are: (1) dogs can be trained to follow commands, making them safe around children, and (2) studies show that people with dogs feel less lonely. Both reasons explain why dogs are good for families.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Reading books is important for children. Books build vocabulary by introducing new words. Reading also strengthens the imagination. In addition, children who read often do better in school.'

Does each sentence after the first one give a reason that supports the main point? Explain.

steps: The main point is: reading books is important for children.
Sentence 2: Books build vocabulary. This supports the point because a bigger vocabulary is important for learning.
Sentence 3: Reading strengthens imagination. This supports the point because imagination helps children learn and grow.
Sentence 4: Children who read often do better in school. This supports the point because doing well in school is important.
All three sentences give reasons that support the main point.
solution.answer: Yes, all three sentences after the first support the main point. Each one gives a specific benefit of reading, which explains why the author says reading is important. The reasons about vocabulary, imagination, and school success all connect back to the main point.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Schools should have recess every day. Moving and playing helps children focus better in class afterward. Exercise is good for growing bodies. Recess also gives children a chance to make friends.

Which reason do you think is the strongest support for the author's point? Why?

steps: The main point is: schools should have recess every day.
Three reasons are given: (1) movement helps children focus better, (2) exercise is good for growing bodies, (3) recess helps children make friends.
Reason 1 is the strongest because it directly connects recess to schoolwork. If recess helps students focus better in class, it clearly benefits the school day.
Reasons 2 and 3 are also valid but less directly tied to the school setting.
solution.answer: The strongest reason is that moving and playing helps children focus better in class afterward. This reason directly connects to school performance, which makes it the best support for the argument that schools should include recess. The other reasons are good but do not directly link recess to classroom success.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Vegetables are an important part of a healthy diet. Vegetables contain vitamins that your body needs to fight sickness. They also have fiber, which helps your digestive system. Eating vegetables can help you stay at a healthy weight.'

A student says the sentence 'They also have fiber, which helps your digestive system' is not a strong reason for the main point. Do you agree? Why or why not?

steps: The main point is that vegetables are important for a healthy diet.
The student says the fiber sentence is not a strong reason.
A healthy diet is supposed to keep your whole body healthy, including your digestive system.
If fiber helps your digestive system, that IS a health benefit, so it does support the main point.
The student is wrong. Fiber supporting digestion is a valid reason because it is a health benefit.
solution.answer: I disagree with the student. The main point is that vegetables are important for a healthy diet. A healthy diet supports all parts of the body, including the digestive system. The reason about fiber directly supports that idea, because a vegetable that helps digestion is helping your health. It is a strong reason.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Libraries are important for communities. They give everyone free access to books, even people who cannot afford to buy them. Libraries also offer computers for people to use. They provide a quiet place to study and learn.'

What is the author's main point? List two reasons the author gives to support it.
items.hint: The main point is usually in the first sentence. The reasons that follow each explain why that first sentence is true.

steps: The main point is: libraries are important for communities.
The author gives three reasons: free access to books, computers for people to use, and a quiet place to study.
Two supporting reasons are: (1) they give free access to books, and (2) they provide computers for people to use.
solution.answer: The author's main point is that libraries are important for communities. Two supporting reasons are: (1) they give everyone free access to books, even people who cannot afford to buy them, and (2) they offer computers for people to use.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Eating breakfast is one of the best things you can do before school. Breakfast gives your brain the energy it needs to think clearly. Students who eat breakfast tend to pay better attention in class. Skipping breakfast can make you feel tired and cranky.'

Which sentence in the passage is the main point? Which reason do you think best supports it? Explain.
items.hint: Find the sentence that the other sentences are trying to prove. Then choose one reason and explain how it connects to that main point.

steps: The main point is the first sentence: eating breakfast is one of the best things before school.
Three reasons follow: energy for the brain, better attention in class, and skipping makes you tired.
The best supporting reason is that students who eat breakfast pay better attention in class.
This directly connects breakfast to success in school, which is what the author is arguing for.
solution.answer: The main point is the first sentence: eating breakfast is one of the best things you can do before school. The best supporting reason is that students who eat breakfast tend to pay better attention in class. This reason supports the main point directly because paying attention in class is a key part of doing well at school.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'People should spend less time looking at screens. Too much screen time can hurt your eyes. It can also make it harder to fall asleep at night. Spending less time on screens leaves more time for outdoor activities and reading.

A student says this sentence is NOT a supporting reason: 'Spending less time on screens leaves more time for outdoor activities and reading.' Do you agree or disagree? Explain.
items.hint: Think about whether the sentence gives a reason WHY people should reduce screen time. Does it support the main point or talk about something else?

steps: The main point is: people should spend less time looking at screens.
The sentence about outdoor activities and reading gives a benefit of spending less time on screens.
If spending less time on screens gives you more time for healthy activities, that is a reason to reduce screen time.
The student is wrong. That sentence does support the main point by showing a positive outcome.
solution.answer: I disagree with the student. The sentence about outdoor activities and reading is a supporting reason because it gives a benefit of reducing screen time. If spending less time on screens gives you more time for active, healthy things, that supports the author's point that people should spend less time on screens.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Planting trees in cities is a great idea. Trees provide shade that keeps streets cool in summer. Their roots absorb rainwater and help prevent flooding. Trees also clean the air by absorbing pollution.'

List all three reasons the author gives and explain how each one supports the main point.
items.hint: For each reason, ask yourself: does this tell me why planting trees in cities is a great idea? If yes, it supports the main point.

steps: Main point: planting trees in cities is a great idea.
Reason 1: trees provide shade that keeps streets cool. This supports the point because cooler streets make cities more comfortable.
Reason 2: roots absorb rainwater and help prevent flooding. This supports the point because preventing flooding keeps cities safe.
Reason 3: trees clean the air by absorbing pollution. This supports the point because cleaner air makes cities healthier.
solution.answer: The author gives three reasons: (1) Trees provide shade that keeps streets cool, supporting the point because comfortable temperatures improve city life. (2) Roots absorb rainwater to prevent flooding, supporting the point because safety is important in cities. (3) Trees clean the air, supporting the point because clean air benefits everyone who lives in the city.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Every child should learn to swim. Swimming is a life-saving skill that can prevent drowning. It is also great exercise for the whole body. Learning to swim builds confidence and helps children feel comfortable in water.'

Are the reasons the author gives convincing? Explain why or why not using at least two reasons from the passage.
items.hint: To decide if a reason is convincing, ask: does it make the main point seem true or important? Does it give facts or benefits that a reader would care about?

steps: Main point: every child should learn to swim.
Reason 1: swimming can prevent drowning. This is very convincing because it involves safety and saving lives.
Reason 2: swimming builds confidence. This is also convincing because confidence is important for children growing up.
Reason 3: it is good exercise. This is a good reason but less powerful than safety.
Overall, the reasons are convincing, especially the safety argument.
solution.answer: Yes, the reasons are convincing. The most convincing reason is that swimming can prevent drowning because it involves life and safety, which are very important. The reason about building confidence is also convincing because it shows swimming has mental benefits as well as physical ones. Together, the reasons show that swimming helps children in multiple important ways.
